predecessors.name: Middle Francia
predecessors.text: Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained Lothair I's after Verdun, with Aachen

successors.name: East Francia
successors.text: eastern Austrasia with Aachen and Metz, most of Frisia and most of Upper Burgundy

successors.name: West Francia
successors.text: west of the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône line, with Lyon, Vienne and Besançon

ledger.x: 855: Lothair I dies and Lothair II inherits the north of Middle Francia.
863: Charles of Provence dies on 24 January and Lothair II takes the Lyonnais and the Viennois, Louis II taking the rest of Provence.
870: The Treaty of Meerssen gives Charles the Bald the west of Lothair's realm.
870: The Treaty of Meerssen gives Louis the German the east.
870: Lothair II's kingdom ends, a year after his death.

wars.name: Succession to Lothair II (Treaty of Meerssen)
wars.outcome: Charles crowned himself at Metz in 869; his brother forced a partition, agreed at Metz in 868 and made at Meerssen on 8 August 870 along roughly the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône.

certainty.note: The partition of 855 names lands (Frisia, Austrasia, Aachen), not a frontier, and the Meerssen line of 870 runs 'roughly' along rivers; the realm 'lacked ethnic or linguistic unity' and its frontiers are approximate throughout.
